content:
The [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Create a professional invoice — line items, tax and totals — then print or download it. Open it and start straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

An invoice generator builds a professional invoice in minutes: your business details, your client's details, line items with quantities and rates, tax, and the total due. Add as many lines as you need, set the tax rate and payment terms, then print the invoice or download it as a file you can send. Everything is filled in and previewed in your browser — nothing is uploaded, stored or sent anywhere, and there is no account to create.

## How to use the Invoice Generator

Open the [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) and start straight away — there is no form to fill in first. The result updates as you work, so you can try different settings and see the change straight away.

1. Fill in your business name and contact details, then your client's name and details.
2. Set the invoice number, the issue date and the due date (or payment terms in days).
3. Add a line for each item: a description, the quantity and the rate. Add or remove lines as needed.
4. Set the tax rate if tax applies, add a short note such as payment details, then print the invoice or download it to send.

## How it works

The [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. A freelance designer invoices a client for 12 hours of design at $75 an hour ($900), plus a $120 stock-photo licence: a subtotal of $1,020, 8% sales tax of $81.60, and a total due of $1,101.60, payable within 14 days. Try the same figures in the [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What to include on an invoice

A complete invoice names both parties, has a unique invoice number and an issue date, lists each item with its quantity and rate, and shows the subtotal, tax and total due. Add a due date and how to pay — bank details, a payment link or a cheque address. A reference such as a project name or purchase order number helps your client match the invoice to their records, and a short note is the place for late-payment terms.

## Getting paid faster

Short payment terms, a clear due date and easy payment details are the three things that speed up payment most. Send the invoice the same day the work is finished, while it is fresh in the client's mind. If a client is late, a polite reminder a few days after the due date works better than waiting a month — and numbering invoices sequentially makes it easy to spot which ones are still open.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Number invoices sequentially (INV-001, INV-002…) so nothing is ever duplicated or missed.
- Always include a due date — invoices without one are paid later on average.
- Keep a copy of every invoice you send, in case a client queries it months later.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is the invoice legally valid?

An invoice you create here is a normal commercial document, but tax and record-keeping rules differ by country and by business type. Check what your tax authority requires — for example, a VAT number where VAT applies — before sending invoices for real transactions. Try it with your own numbers in the [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I download the invoice?

Yes. Use Download to save the invoice as a file you can email or store, or Print to print it (or save it as a PDF from your browser's print dialogue). Try it with your own numbers in the [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my client data saved anywhere?

No. Everything you type stays in your browser and is never uploaded or stored. Close the page and it is gone, so download the invoice before you leave. You can use it as often as you like, and because nothing is uploaded, stored or tracked, there is nothing to delete afterwards.

### Is the Invoice Generator free to use?

Yes. The Invoice Generator is free to use as often as you like, with no sign-up. There is no limit on how often you use it, nothing to install, and no account to create — open the [Invoice Generator](/invoice-generator) and start straight away.

### How accurate is the Invoice Generator?

The result follows directly from the values you enter. Treat it as an estimate for informational use, and check important figures against an authoritative source. For figures that matter, such as money, health or legal deadlines, check the result against an authoritative source before acting on it.
